title: Reversing a boolean vector is an involution
statement: For any boolean vector $v = (v_0, v_1, \ldots, v_{n-1})$ of length $n \ge 1$, reversing its coordinate order twice returns the original vector: if $v'$ denotes the vector obtained by reversing the coordinate order of $v$, then reversing the coordinate order of $v'$ recovers $v$ exactly.
hypotheses_covered: v is a boolean vector of length n (with n a positive natural number)
replaced: Reversing a boolean vector twice recovers it.
